title: Add luminous Line numbers with conditional visibility and crystal clearance
body:
Prism numbers now appear for selected, highlighted, hovered or keyboard-focused Lines. The browser-local **Show all numbers** control reveals every physical number and remembers that choice. Clearing one visibility reason keeps the number visible while another still applies, including touch selection.

Implements #26 on the integrated artwork in [PR #58](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/pull/58). This PR is stacked on its renderer branch so the review shows the numbering change. Acceptance and merge remain dependent on #53; retarget and renew affected evidence after that source merges.

The placement helper measures the live font and reserves at least a 24-by-24-pixel click envelope with 11-pixel minimum text. It uses final crystal, connector and interaction-ring dimensions through the actual screen transform. It places all numbers together before visibility is applied, preventing labels from moving when selection or hover changes. A bounded search and explicit fallback keep unexpected layouts usable without shrinking text or knowingly showing collisions. A hidden canvas defers measurement until it is visible. The compact toolbar keeps the legend above the inspector.

The new helper has one explicit local asset route and joins the existing runtime inclusion lists. Windows upgrade fixtures now check the copied wall and all three JavaScript files against their source hashes. The physical writer, task epochs, assignments, modes, scenes, unread state, tray artwork and services retain their existing behavior.

## Validation

Candidate `fb723f2a04b7804b716ea9ed88bcef5bc44e23a0`, based on `d978392889e408713be6a9badfbad822c38b970c`. The recorded browser, Python and workflow evidence applies to this source.

- Full local browser suite passes, retaining all 360 raw number clicks and prior application/renderer journeys. Independent DOM measurements cover 720 labels across 48 combinations of 1440/800/390-pixel widths, four rotations and both flips. They check real text and hit bounds against crystal bodies, connector polygons, selection/highlight/pending rings, other labels and canvas edges.
- Added journeys cover visibility unions, a touch-capable browser tap, persistent show-all, neutral cores and stable accessible names across Work/Quiet/Free and reduced motion, missing-label-asset repair, zero-size hidden canvases, unchanged label positions, and passive requests. Existing assembly interruption, associations, geometry replacement, keyboard/modifier selection and explicit Locate checks remain.
- Six Node test entries pass, including the 48-case pure geometry matrix, deterministic output, separate connector/Line identity namespaces, impossible canvases and search limits. The actual fixture used at most 16 of 50,000 search nodes. This does not establish support for 300 Lines.
- The full Python suite passes 161 tests, including protected asset serving and an isolated foreground Linux package. SVG exports are unchanged and reproducible. Workflow checks pass seven current specifications and eight complete archives, with ten workflow tests. `gh-26-prism-numerals` is synchronized and archived.
- Nine 2× pixel-density captures cover default, multiple-selected and show-all states at desktop, compact and mobile widths. Desktop/mobile selections and the compact show-all view were inspected. Chromium headless shell 149.0.7827.55 ran the local browser checks through the documented executable override. These captures still need human approval.

Observed failures were retained before correction: all 15 idle numbers shown by default; compact neighbouring-ring clearance; zero-size hidden canvas measurement; and compact legend overlap. The fixes pass the complete current browser suite.

## Delivery gates and handoffs

Both final independent Standards and Specification reviews are clear with no P0–P3 findings. Normal merges incorporate the renderer's native visibility fix and slow-frame test corrections. The complete final local browser suite passes again, including all 720 DOM label measurements. Negative checks reject stale visibility state, a phase reset and failed resume scheduling. All nine current-head hosted jobs passed in [PR run `34427995718`](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/actions/runs/34427995718), including both Windows Python/isolated upgrade fixtures. The run identifies PR #60 and this exact head. Human approval of the current integrated UI remains pending. Guarded merge, main CI, guide synchronization and issue readback remain required. Issue completion follows the remaining guide and verification gates.

The separately owned [Linux PR #57](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/pull/57) must copy `prism.js`, `prism-adapters.js` and `prism-labels.js` alongside the wall when reconciling this source. Guide synchronization is tracked in [Hub PR #82](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/pull/82). No installation, physical-light operation or public guide publication is part of this PR.

title: Support a fresh Linux installation of Nanoleaf services
body:
Adds a fresh Linux installation of the existing Nanoleaf services. Hooks, CLI, wall map and controller share private Linux SQLite; the existing on-demand worker remains the sole light writer. The separate Node MCP host uses its existing direct HTTP transport. Linux runtime commands no longer need Windows executable forwarding.

Implements #54. Installed WSL, real-client and physical acceptance remains #55. [Hub PR #84](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/pull/84) is the architecture/work-guide companion for Hub #43. Guide synchronization remains pending until that PR merges. This does not import old data, change the wall presentation, add a combined daemon or hook API, or adopt shared monitoring.

The installer creates a private Python environment, copies the required runtime and selected native Node 24, builds the pinned MCP package, preserves unrelated hooks, accepts configured Desktop JSON paths, and generates three user service units. It starts no services or worker and sends only a device layout read. The operator must retire the Windows owner before activating Linux hooks or services. Defaults are wall 8765, controller 41231 and MCP 41230. Port collisions fail visibly; Linux map commands print their URL.

Validation:

- Focused failing-then-passing tests cover explicit hook/setup state selection, fixed map ports, duplicate owners and stale receipts, private installer state, bounded token input, runtime/hook generation, credential separation, service definitions and MCP port collisions.
- The complete isolated installer ran with real venv/pip/npm and a loopback fake Nanoleaf device. Separate installed foreground services served the wall map and authenticated controller/MCP requests. Eight worker processes respected an existing exclusive lock. MCP Quiet/Work/Free commands settled and restored the fake scene and brightness.
- Local checks pass: 173 Python tests at current head `7c06f6555050ffe058be9493a71a7de9f5cc94e0`. The 39 MCP tests with build/type/artifact checks passed at `4abafec`; the subsequent two-file change only corrects the Python installer filesystem guard and its regression test. Browser checks using the documented override and cached Chromium headless shell, workflow checks with seven specifications and ten workflow tests, and static systemd unit verification passed before the focused filesystem/description fixes; those areas are unchanged. Loopback was excluded from the task's HTTP proxy for local checks.
- All 18 configured push/PR checks passed at the prior head `b1653cf8522f8df65302a0bb7ac11fe7fb4575a1`, including hosted Windows and browser jobs. GitHub refused to start all 18 current-head jobs because of an account payment or spending-limit problem. Current-head CI must pass before merge. No local Windows, ordinary-WSL systemd, actual Codex client or physical-light acceptance is claimed.

The issue-linked OpenSpec change `gh-54-linux-fresh-install` is synchronized and archived. Independent Standards and Specification reviews have no P0–P3 findings at base/merge-base `cdceffddb7a86c138797325e8d6b0460eb320e58` and head `7c06f6555050ffe058be9493a71a7de9f5cc94e0`. Specification verifies A1–A7. See the [final review receipt](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/pull/57#issuecomment-5610892283). The installer/ownership ADR is `docs/decisions/0007-linux-runtime-ownership.md`; operator instructions are `docs/linux-install.md`. The current main connector-geometry change is retained.
